title: Ant-Man
synopsis: Scott Lang takes on a dangerous assignment from Hank Pym while trying to rebuild his relationship with his daughter Cassie.
verdictRationale: Scott’s willingness to risk his life for Cassie is admirable. The film also makes burglaries entertaining and gives Scott’s crew little accountability.
ageRationale: A man is reduced to a small mass by experimental technology, and the film includes gunfire, profanity and a sedative reference.
reflection: A father’s repentance takes shape through choices he makes after the promise to change. Ask what Scott can do to rebuild trust through daily reliability as well as extraordinary courage.

title: Avengers: Age of Ultron
synopsis: Tony Stark and Bruce Banner help create Ultron, whose plan to save humanity places civilians in danger.
verdictRationale: Civilians matter to the Avengers even when rescue complicates their mission. The film also puts much of its energy into violent spectacle and leaves its heroes’ accountability unsettled.
ageRationale: Large-scale destruction, an arm torn off, a major death, profanity and innuendo merit teen guidance.
reflection: Tony’s fear helps explain why he acts without patience or consultation. A family can ask what humility would look like when a powerful person is motivated by real danger.

title: Captain America: Civil War
synopsis: A plan to regulate the Avengers divides the team while a hidden adversary exploits old grief.
verdictRationale: The film takes accountability and conscience seriously. Grief and revenge push friends toward violence, and the split remains painful.
ageRationale: Intense combat, drowning, and a violent revelation about a family death make this better suited to teens.
reflection: People can owe accountability and still deserve mercy. Tony’s grief and Steve’s loyalty give families a place to talk about truthfulness before a conflict hardens.

title: Doctor Strange
synopsis: A surgeon seeks healing after a crash and becomes a sorcerer defending Earth against a threat from another dimension.
verdictRationale: Stephen’s growth in humility has value. This draft weighs the film’s sustained presentation of sorcery as a path to healing, power and saving others as the dominant spiritual concern.
ageRationale: An implied beheading, surgical peril, repeated attacks and frightening supernatural imagery warrant teen guidance apart from the spiritual verdict.
reflection: Stephen starts out evaluating people by what they can do for him. Families can reflect on the change from pride to service and discuss why spiritual healing in Christian life is grounded in Christ.

biblicalParallels.title: A kingdom’s responsibilities beyond its borders
biblicalParallels.filmMoment: T’Challa moves toward Nakia’s call to share Wakanda’s resources after confronting the harms of isolation.
biblicalParallels.reflection: Paul’s call to attend to others’ interests helps families consider T’Challa’s decision to serve beyond Wakanda. The question applies wherever a community has gifts others could benefit from.

questions: Why does Nakia leave Wakanda to help people elsewhere?
What gives Killmonger’s criticism force?
What does T’Challa learn about his father’s choices?
How are Nakia’s and Killmonger’s responses to suffering different?
Which resources could your family share with people beyond your usual circle?

findings: T’Challa and Nakia kiss, and some characters wear revealing evening clothes.
The guide reports profanity in dialogue and music.
Ritual combat and battles include stabbings, shootings and a throat cutting.
Wakandans invoke Bast and visit an ancestral plane after consuming a ritual preparation.
Alcohol is consumed at the casino, and a fictional plant preparation is used in the coronation ritual.
Nakia pushes Wakanda to use its resources beyond its borders, while Killmonger pursues violent retaliation.
